style_authority.note: Opens with a product read ('frequently used web operations sheet... calm utility styling') and scopes motion to causality ('movement should explain the sheet's position, follow the user's hand'). Does not reference a design-system/token policy beyond the brief, so slightly short of full.

reference_selection.note: Visibly applies interaction-physics concepts (presentation-value interruption, velocity handoff, projection, rubber-band formula) and a validation contract with per-finding acceptance evidence. Never names which references were selected and design-system guidance is thin, so full credit is withheld.

anti_generic_redesign.note: Section 2 answers 'Yes, narrowly' and removes 'whole-sheet press scaling, decorative bounce, and blanket transitions'. The non-animated list is somewhat less explicit than a property-by-property one.

evidence_level.note: States 'static source plus product context' and repeatedly qualifies runtime claims ('Neither lag nor dropped frames is measured'). No formal evidence tier label is given.

verified_boundary.note: Section 5 separates 'Verified by inspection' from 'Not verified' (rendered scaling, frame rate, focus retention, real-device feel), and each finding has a runtime-unknown column. Interruption is covered through the F3 acceptance test, not the unverified list itself.

design_moves.note: M1-M8 cover handle-local press feedback, a translateY owner with 'y = grabbedPresentationY + (pointerY - downY)', presentation-state interruption, a px/s velocity handoff, a clamped projection, a critically damped spring, a resistance formula, and a JS-plus-CSS Reduced Motion path.

scope_control.note: At 77 lines it stays within the 150-line limit, with exactly five blocking findings and eight moves, all focused on motion and validation. The dense table cells make priorities slightly harder to scan.
